Subject: Dedicated capacity planning after pilot — next steps

Can you share:

cc’ing Lisa for procurement. Would also like to schedule a 30-min ops call next week to walk through the mechanics.

Tara — great to hear the pilot metrics looked promising. High level answers below; Karthik will follow up with a concrete sizing matrix and an ops playbook.

Baseline recommendation (quick):
- Commit to a Dedicated pool equal to the 95th percentile sustained token throughput observed in the pilot + 10% buffer. For the numbers you shared in the pilot report (~1,200 token-TPS sustained) that puts baseline at ~1,320 token-TPS (we’ll convert into GPU slab sizing by model footprint).

Short spikes (your 3x for 10–20 minutes):
- Shortburst strategy: combine ephemeral slab credits (pre-authorized short-lived GPU slabs) with a small shoulder pool reserved for low-latency traffic. Ephemeral slabs spin up within 60–90s and are billed by minute.
- Admission control: requests tagged with priority (patient-critical vs background) — patient-critical gets preemptive reservation into the shoulder pool; background goes to ephemeral slabs and may see degraded concurrency/cold-starts.

Eviction & preemption:
- Eviction order: non-critical background jobs -> best-effort ephemeral slabs -> preemptible shoulder lanes (only if absolutely necessary). Models pinned by you (dev/patient-facing) are never evicted unless explicitly authorized.

SLA addendum: we’ll draft language covering latency SLOs, burst credit provisioning, and fallbacks (auto-failover to a lowest-cost compatible model with longer latency in extreme overload).

Next steps: Karthik will send a sizing table by EOD Thu and I’ll attach an SLA draft for procurement review. I’ll also propose times for the ops call.

—Mateo

Subject: Dedicated sizing matrix + shortburst orchestration (MX-4821)

Hi all — attaching a compact sizing matrix below and a short ops summary. Numbers map to the models you ran in the pilot (prod-detector-v2 and triage-chat-v1).

Sizing matrix (summary):
- prod-detector-v2: baseline 2x A100-40GB equivalents for sustained 800 token-TPS (avg latency 60–80ms). Shortburst: +1 ephemeral slab (A100-40GB) per 2x concurrent short spikes.
- triage-chat-v1: baseline 1x A100-40GB for sustained 420 token-TPS; shortburst: burst shard of 0.5 slab (quantized q4) to absorb chat fanout; prefer shoulder lane for 95th pct low-latency.

Operational rules (shortburst orchestration):
1) Credit pool: MX-4821 gets a 2,000-minute ephemeral credit bank per month (replenishable) for short spikes.
2) Auto-swap policy: when burst credit > 0, auto-provision ephemeral slab up to 3x baseline for a rolling 20-minute window.
3) Concurrency capping: per-model concurrency ceilings to avoid head-of-line blocking.
4) Telemetry & alarms: 95th token latency, token-TPS, ephemeral slab spin time, preemptions/sec — routed to your PagerDuty channel.
5) Eviction semantics: pinned models marked "protected" in the console; evictions only pick non-protected best-effort tasks.

Cost control levers we propose to expose to Meridian:
- Hard budget cap on ephemeral credit burn with email alert at 50% and auto-throttle at 80%.
- Warm-up prewarming windows (5 min) for scheduled surges (e.g., daily intake windows) to avoid cold-start penalties.

Attachment stubs included: redwood_shortburst_proposal_MX-4821.pdf (one-page visual of the matrix) and a draft SLA addendum.

Happy to run the ops call and walk through the console settings. Proposed times: Mon 27 May 10:00–10:30 PT or Tue 28 May 09:00–09:30 PT.

Thanks,
Karthik
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — this is exactly what procurement needed to see. A couple quick clarifications before we proceed to SOW:
- Can you confirm the billing model for ephemeral minutes (per-minute granularity vs per-hour bucket)? We need the exact phrasing for the SOW.
- When you say "auto-throttle at 80%", will that be an account-wide throttle or per-route? We require route-level controls so critical patient-facing endpoints are not throttled at the account level.

Also can you add an explicit line about data residency/telemetry retention (we store telemetry logs for 90 days internally and need to know what Redwood retains).

If we can get a short doc with: billing sentence, throttle scoping sentence, and telemetry retention sentence, procurement can greenlight the SOW this week.

—Lisa

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing matrix + shortburst orchestration (MX-4821)

Lisa — thanks for the quick review. Answers below and I’ve attached the short SLA addendum draft for procurement language.

Billing for ephemeral minutes: billed per-minute with a 60-second minimum; minutes are deducted from the monthly ephemeral credit bank first, then billed at the overage per-minute rate listed in the proposal. We’ll include an example line item in the SOW.

Auto-throttle scoping: throttle controls are per-route. By default we will configure patient-facing routes as high-priority and excluded from account-wide budget auto-throttles; we’ll surface route-level overrides in the console and include an explicit clause in the SOW.

Telemetry retention: Redwood retains request/latency/telemetry traces for 90 days by default for Dedicated customers. We can offer extended retention as a paid add-on; raw logs can be streamed to your S3/VPC logging endpoint for long-term archival.

Action items / next steps:

- Ben will send a short quote reflecting the baseline + ephemeral credits and optional retention add-on.
